title: Tenant schedules, SLA/SLO comms & Terraform upgrade cheat-sheet
summary: Working kit of email/Slack templates, timezone-aware maintenance scheduling guidance, SLA/SLO language snippets for customer contracts, and a concise Terraform module upgrade checklist and commands for private (VPC/on-prem) customers.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, shareable kit for the Private Deployments team to use when preparing and executing maintenance/upgrade windows for tenant-managed environments (VPC and on-prem customers). It combines: quick SLA/SLO framing for customer comms, timezone-aware scheduling guidance, escalation contacts and an operational one-hour rollback plan, plus a short Terraform module/upgrade checklist and commands that are safe for customer-run ops.

Audience:
- Solutions / Customer Ops reps who craft customer notices
- SRE / Runbook authors executing upgrades with customers
- Customer engineering contacts (for on-prem/VPC)
- Sales/Legal reference for SLA language during negotiation (short form)

Quick rules-of-thumb (ops):
- Standard advance notice: 30 days for major upgrades; 7 days for minor (non-invasive) upgrades; 72 hours for targeted config changes; 2 hours for emergency maintenance only when required.
- Work windows: prefer customer local low-traffic windows (typically 01:00-05:00 local time). If multiple tenants, coordinate using a shared availability matrix.
- Canary progression: 10% -> 35% -> 100% (or node count: 1 -> 3 -> all), wait 30–60 minutes between phases and run smoke/latency checks.
- SLA impact communication: be explicit about expected customer downtime (if any) and degraded performance windows.

SLA / SLO snippets (short, copy-paste friendly):
- For customer comms (simple): "Redwood Inference will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain availability of the private control plane and inference endpoints in accordance with the agreed SLA. For planned maintenance, customers will be notified as detailed below; brief interruptions may occur but Redwood will minimize impact by using staged rollouts and automatic fallbacks."
- For contract/legal (concise clause): "Service Availability: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a monthly availability of 99.9% for hosted control-plane services managing private deployments. Availability excludes scheduled maintenance windows (customers will be notified at least 30 days in advance for major upgrades and may be required to approve on-prem upgrade windows). Credits for availability shortfalls will be provided per the agreed SLA schedule."
- SLO examples (engineering/ops): "Control plane availability: 99.95% monthly; Inference endpoint P99 latency: <= 250ms for single-turn requests under normal load; Job scheduling/management API success rate: >= 99.9%"

Customer communication templates
1) 30-day Advance Notice (major upgrade) - Email subject and body
Subject: [Action Required] Planned platform upgrade for your Redwood deployment — schedule inside
Body: Hi <Customer Name>,
We plan a major maintenance upgrade for your Redwood deployment (release vX.Y -> vX.Z) that includes kernel updates and optional model runtime improvements. Proposed window: <local date, start-end>. Expected customer impact: brief rolling restart of control-plane agents; inference endpoints will remain available via fallback for the majority of traffic but some requests may experience elevated latency (~50–200ms) during staged rollout.
What we need from you: please confirm the proposed window within 7 business days or provide an alternate within that week. If you require us to run the upgrade outside the proposed window, we can coordinate a dedicated maintenance engagement.
If you have any concerns, reply to this thread or contact: primary-ops@example.com, escalation: eng-oncall@example.com.
Thanks,
Redwood Private Deployments

2) 72-hour Reminder (minor, non-invasive change) - Slack + Email snippet
Slack (to customer channel): Heads-up: We’ll apply a configuration tweak to your routing policy on <date/time local>. No expected downtime; we’ll post progress updates.
Email (short): Friendly reminder: config change for <component> in 72 hours. Reach out if this conflicts.

3) Emergency/Out-of-band brief (when forced)
Subject: [URGENT] Immediate maintenance for your Redwood deployment — short downtime expected
Body: We’re applying an immediate emergency fix to address a critical issue affecting inference latency. Expected disruption: ~5–15 minutes of degraded responses while service restarts. We will: 1) run the hotfix on a single node 2) monitor for 15 minutes 3) proceed with rolling patch if metrics are stable. Contact: oncall-privatelayer@example.com (phone: +1-415-555-0192).

Escalation & Contacts (matrix)
- Primary ops lead: Asha Kapoor — asha.kapoor@redwood.ai — availability: M-F 08:00–18:00 PT
- Secondary SRE: Marco Ruiz — marco.ruiz@redwood.ai — on-call pager for emergencies
- Eng on-call escalation: eng-oncall@example.com — routes to SRE rotation
- Customer success manager: Priya Nair — priya.nair@redwood.ai
- Legal/compliance: legal-support@example.com (for SLA disputes)

Pre-upgrade customer checklist (send 7 days prior)
- Confirm maintenance window and time zone (include calendar invite)
- Provide point-of-contact (name + phone + Slack channel) for the upgrade execution
- Confirm backup status and restore verification steps on customer side (if on-prem)
- Confirm whether auto-failover/cutover procedures are permitted for the tenant
- Share estimated maintenance duration and known risks

Day-of runbook (short)
1) Kickoff: 10 minutes pre-window, confirm POC and channel; record runbook owner
2) Canary stage: upgrade single node or dedicated canary host; run smoke tests (latency, successful inference, KV cache priming)
3) Monitor metrics for 30 minutes: P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, disk io
4) If stable -> progress to staged rollouts, if not -> initiate rollback plan (see below)
5) Final verification: run 3 representative end-to-end prompts and validate outputs against baseline evals (automated script if available)
6) Post-mortem/notes to customer within 24 hours

One-hour rollback plan (emergency safe path)
Goal: return customer to pre-upgrade state within 60 minutes from rollback decision.
Steps:
- Immediately stop rollout and mark impacted nodes as maintenance
- Reapply prior agent/container image via the module variable: ri_private_agent_image = "vX.Y.Z"
- If using Terraform: terraform apply -var-file=rollback.tfvars --target=module.private_agents  (pre-created rollback tfvars commits image pin)
- Restart control-plane services in reverse order of upgrade (control plane first, then agents)
- Run smoke tests and confirm baseline metrics; if still failing escalate to engineering on-call

Terraform module notes (cheat-sheet)
- Module canonical name: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//private_deploy (example)
- Recommended pinned versions: start with module v1.2.x for patches; use v1.3.0+ for kernel/runtime upgrades after internal validation
- Useful vars (prefix ri_private_): ri_private_agent_image, ri_private_agent_count, ri_private_rolling_batch_size, ri_private_canary_node_ids, ri_private_kms_key
- Best practice: do not change ri_private_agent_image and ri_private_rolling_batch_size in the same apply. Two-step approach reduces blast radius.
- Example safe upgrade sequence (CLI):
  - git checkout release-branch
  - update module version in modules.tf: module "private_deploy" { source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//private_deploy?ref=v1.3.0" }
  - terraform init -upgrade
  - terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars -out=upgrade.plan
  - terraform apply "upgrade.plan"
- Useful commands to evaluate drift and expected changes:
  - terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars | sed -n '1,200p'  # quick view, pipe to file for review
  - terraform state list | grep private_agents
  - terraform apply --target=module.private_deploy.module.agent_pool  # target small subset for canary

Post-upgrade verification checklist
- Automated smoke tests pass (3/3)
- Latency: P95 within 20% of baseline, P99 within target SLO
- Error rate < 0.1% for management APIs
- Logs show no critical warnings related to KV cache or kernel mismatches
- Customer confirms sanity-check prompts and approves final signoff

Notes on customer-managed on-prem caveats
- Network egress rules often block outbound telemetry; confirm customer allowed endpoints before rolling upgrades (list telemetry/metrics endpoints in the advance email)
- KMS/HSM integrations: if upgrade touches crypto libs, coordinate with customer's security team 2 weeks out
- Airgapped installs: follow airgap artifact staging checklist in Confluence (linked artifact above) and allow extra validation time (minimum +48 hours)

Sample Slack status cadence during rollout
- 00:00 Kickoff — Starting canary stage on node <id>
- +15m Canary checks: OK (attach smoke results) or FAIL (reason)
- +45m Staged rollout: 30% nodes updated — monitoring
- +90m Final: rollout complete — post-verification in progress

Post-mortem/Customer note template (24 hours)
Subject: Summary — Maintenance for <date> (vX.Y -> vX.Z)
Body: Hi <Customer>,
Summary: Completed planned upgrade on <date>. Staged rollout, no customer-visible downtime; P99 latency briefly elevated during canary by ~120ms for 18 minutes. Root cause: required cache warmup after kernel patch.
Actions taken: performed rollback on one node during canary, re-applied image pin for that node, repeated canary with warmed cache, proceeded to full rollout.
Next steps: we will add cache-warmup script to canary step and include in next release notes.

Appendix: Helpful quick links and check commands for on-call
- Run smoke: scripts/priv_upgrade_smoke.sh <customer-id>
- Fetch recent errors: kubectl -n <ns> logs -l app=private-agent --since=60m | grep -i error
- Terraform drift check: terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars

End of kit. Use and adapt templates, keep customer wording conservative (less technical for stakeholder-facing comms, more technical for POC-level comms). This doc is intentionally compact — expand to customer-specific runbooks where needed.
